copyBody: Type your text and every leaf preset updates live. Press Copy beside the row you want and paste it into the destination. The 🍃 🍂 🍁 leaves are emoji, while ❧ ❦ ˚ and ✿ are ordinary Unicode symbols, so a leaf font generator result keeps its leaves in a bio, display name, caption or message without any font installed on the other end, and the cursive letters survive for the same reason.
popular: Each leaf carries a season. The 🍃 green leaf around cursive script (🍃 𝒜𝓊𝓉𝓊𝓂𝓃 𝒜𝒾𝓇 🍃) is spring and summer, and the everyday choice for plant and nature bios. The 🍂 fallen leaves are the autumn frame and the most pasted leaf style every September and October. The 🍁 maple is autumn too, and doubles as the Canadian flag leaf. The ❧ text leaf is the monochrome option for places that reject emoji, and the 🍃 ˚ drifting frame adds a trailing mark like a leaf letting go.

socialTitle: Leaf Fonts for Instagram and Fall Captions
social: Leaf text peaks in autumn. Every fall, 🍂 and 🍁 frames fill Instagram bios, TikTok display names, Pinterest boards and captions for pumpkin-patch, sweater-weather and Thanksgiving posts. The rest of the year the 🍃 green leaf carries plant, garden, eco and wellness accounts, and the 🍁 maple marks Canadian bios year-round. Display names and bios accept every row on this page. Actual @usernames are stricter almost everywhere, so keep the handle plain and put the leaves in the display name.
limitNote: the leaf emoji are drawn differently on iPhone, Android and Windows, while the ❧ ❦ text leaves look the same everywhere.
specificTitle: Leaf Font Generator vs Vine Fonts
specific: Leaf, vine and flower frames overlap and this site has a page for each. A leaf font generator uses single leaves that read as a season: green for spring, brown and maple for autumn. Vine text uses tendrils and climbing shapes that read as engraved or grown-over, and flower text uses blossoms. If the name is about a season or a single sprig, start here; for invitations and botanical brands, the vine page is closer.

uniqueBody: The three leaf emoji are not interchangeable, and a leaf font generator is most useful when you match the leaf to the moment. 🍃 (leaf fluttering in wind) is green and drawn with motion lines on most platforms, which makes it read as fresh air, spring and plants. 🍂 (fallen leaf) is brown and usually drawn as two or three leaves, the unmistakable autumn mark. 🍁 (maple leaf) is red, reads as autumn in most places and as Canada in others, so it does double duty for Canadian accounts.

The ❧ text leaf is different in kind. It is a monochrome printer's ornament, one character wide, and it inherits the text colour, so it works in places emoji cannot: game name fields, plain-text signatures, older forums and anywhere a 🍃 would show as a box. Its upright twin ❦ is on this page too, and the pair reads as a vine when both are used.

Lettering follows the season. Cursive script beside 🍂 or 🍁 is the fall pairing that fills captions every October. Bold cursive stands up to the green of the 🍃 in a display name. Italic with a ✿ or a ☾ ☽ moon drifts toward cottagecore and night-garden looks, and the 🌿 🍄 forest-floor row is for woodland and mushroom accounts. Preview the exact name you plan to use before you copy.

faqs: Online, a leaf font means text decorated with leaf symbols or emoji, such as 🍂 𝒩𝒶𝓂𝑒 🍂 or ❧ Name ❧. It is Unicode text you can copy and paste, not an installed typeface.
Is this leaf font generator free?
Yes. It runs in your browser, needs no account or download, and every result can be copied without limits.
Which leaf is the autumn one?
🍂 is the fallen-leaf emoji and reads as autumn everywhere. 🍁 is the maple leaf, which reads as autumn in most places and as Canada in others.
Is there a text-only leaf symbol?
Yes. The ❧ and ❦ floral-heart dingbats are monochrome leaf ornaments that render in every font. Both are on this page.
Why does the leaf look different on my friend's phone?
Emoji are drawn by each platform, so the leaves on iOS, Android and Windows are different illustrations. The ❧ text leaf looks the same everywhere.
